articles.title: Familial Budd-Chiari Syndrome in China: A Systematic Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract: Familial occurrence of Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) has been reported in scattered cases, which potentially favors the congenital theory. A review of the literature was conducted to demonstrate this phenomenon in China. PubMed, VIP, and CNKI databases were searched for studies describing at least two Chinese BCS patients from the same one family. In the 18 eligible papers, 30 siblings or first-degree relatives from 14 families were diagnosed with BCS at 9 different centers. Common clinical presentations included varices of abdominal wall and lower limbs, edema of legs, and ascites. Type and location of obstruction were similar among these patients from the same one family. Screening for BCS was conducted in 65 family members from 3 families, demonstrating that 2 asymptomatic siblings from one family were further diagnosed with BCS. Factor V Leiden mutation was found in 3 of 4 patients from one family and in one of 2 patients from another one family. Prothrombin G20210A gene mutation was found in none of the 4 patients from the 2 families. In conclusion, our study showed the possibility of familial aggregation in Chinese BCS patients, but these available data cannot support the previous hypothesis that familial BCS originates from congenital vascular malformation.

articles.title: Cutaneous vascular lesions.
articles.abstract: In 1982, vascular anomalies were classified as either vascular tumors or vascular malformations. Hemangiomas were identified as benign tumors that undergo a phase of active growth characterized by endothelial proliferation and hypercellularity, followed by gradual tumor regression over the first decade. Vascular malformations were described as structural congenital anomalies derived from capillaries, veins, lymphatic vessels, arteries, or a combination of these. Unlike vascular tumors, vascular malformations were shown to have normal levels of endothelial turnover and to grow proportionately with the child. This article describes the most common types of vascular anomalies and available treatment modalities.

articles.title: Conus medullaris-cauda arteriovenous malformation and Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome: what is the treatment goal?
articles.abstract: A 29-year-old man with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) presented with a symptomatic conus medullaris-cauda arteriovenous malformation (AVM) manifesting as back and right limb pain, which abruptly worsened with the onset of right limb weakness and urinary retention. He was treated by multisession endovascular embolization resulting in improved neurological status. KTS is a sporadic disease with unknown etiology, but genetic susceptibility may lead to the over-expression of angiogenic factors and increased angiogenesis. KTS may be exceptionally associated with slow-flow spinal AVM, but there is no consensus about the optimal treatment for these symptomatic lesions. Embolization treatment may represent a safe option to minimize complications and possibly improve the neurological status in patients with spinal AVM associated with KTS, if one or both legs are already impaired by hypertrophy or other vascular malformations. Genetic analysis may reveal an underlying angiogenesis change, so closer follow up might be indicated in selected patients.

articles.title: Syndromes associated with vascular tumors and malformations: a pictorial review.
articles.abstract: Use of the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) classification system has been strongly recommended in recent years because of the need for separate therapeutic measures for patients with vascular tumors and malformations. In the ISSVA classification system, vascular tumors, which are neoplastic, are distinguished from vascular malformations, which are caused by vascular structural anomalies and are not neoplastic, on the basis of the presence or absence of neoplastic proliferation of vascular endothelial cells. It is important that radiologists be familiar with the development, diagnosis, and treatment of vascular tumors and malformations, especially the imaging features of low- and high-flow vascular malformations. Some vascular tumors and malformations develop in isolation, whereas others develop within the phenotype of a syndrome. Syndromes that are associated with vascular tumors include PHACE syndrome. Syndromes that are associated with vascular malformations include Sturge-Weber, Klippel-Trénaunay, Proteus, blue rubber bleb nevus, Maffucci, and Gorham-Stout syndromes, all of which demonstrate low flow, and Rendu-Osler-Weber, Cobb, Wyburn-Mason, and Parkes Weber syndromes, all of which demonstrate high flow. Because imaging findings may help identify such syndromes as systemic, it is important that radiologists familiarize themselves with these conditions.

articles.title: [Medical care of brain malformative vascular diseases discovered during the pre- or neonatal period].
articles.abstract: Three types of brain arteriovenous vascular malformations can be found during the neonatal period, according to their anatomical location. Vein of Galen malformations are the most common. The others are pial arteriovenous malformations or dural arteriovenous malformations, which include dural sinus malformations. They can be asymptomatic, but most often they are associated with different symptoms, related to their angioarchitecture or their effect on the brain. High-flow arteriovenous malformations can thus be responsible for heart failure. Local or regional venous hyperpressure exposes the patient to subacute or chronic brain lesions, or to hydrovenous disorders such as hydrocephalus. Some types of venous reflux can expose patients to brain hemorrhage. The treatment chosen for these vascular malformations and their consequences is transarterial or transvenous embolization, depending on the angioarchitecture and type of lesion. The schedule for the treatment will be determined according to the malformation type and its local or general effects on the brain. The aim of this article is to present the recommendations of the French National Referral Center for neurovascular malformations in children, in order to help clinicians and radiologists treat these patients during pre- or neonatal period.

articles.title: Gamma Knife Radiosurgery of Surgically Partially Resected Cerebral Arteriovenous Malformations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In this study, we aimed to evaluate flow characteristics in partially resected arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) and identify factors associated with complete obliteration following Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS).
METHODS: Among 587 patients with AVMs treated with GKRS between August 1992 and October 2024, 31 patients with residual AVMs after microsurgical resection were included. Clinical charts and imaging studies were retrospectively reviewed. AVM flow was categorized as low, moderate, or high based on the number of angiographic frames from nidus visualization to draining vein opacification. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to estimate complete obliteration rates, while univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were applied to identify factors associated with complete obliteration. The log-rank test was used to compare actuarial complete obliteration rates among the three AVM flow groups.
RESULTS: The median clinical follow-up period after GKRS was 44 months (interquartile range, 35-105). Complete obliteration was achieved in 24 patients (77.4%). The actuarial obliteration rates were 29.0%, 56.7%, and 69.7% at 3, 5, and 10 years, respectively. Complete obliteration occurred in three (37.5%) high-flow, 14 (87.5%) moderate-flow, and all low-flow AVMs. The mean time to obliteration was 131.7 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 92.9-170.6) for high-flow AVMs, 73.0 months (95% CI, 44.2-101.8) for moderate-flow AVMs, and 36.7 months (95% CI, 22.1-51.3) for low-flow AVMs (p=0.004, log-rank test). Prior embolization and lower AVM flow were independently associated with complete obliteration on both univariate and multivariate analyses.
CONCLUSION: GKRS produced favorable outcomes in patients with partially resected AVMs. Slower-flow residual AVMs and prior embolization were independently associated with higher rates of complete obliteration.

articles.title: Bilateral persistent sciatic arteries with right sciatic artery aneurysm and thromboembolism: a case report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: Persistent sciatic artery (PSA) is a rare congenital vascular anomaly. Bilateral complete-type PSA complicated by aneurysm and thromboembolism is particularly uncommon, with limited reports in the literature. Herein, we present a case of bilateral complete-type PSA with right sciatic artery (SA) aneurysm and thromboembolism to improve clinicians' awareness of this rare vascular variant and its management.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 79-year-old woman presented with sudden-onset right calf pain for 2 days, which had worsened over the past day. An outpatient vascular ultrasound suggested an incomplete occlusion of the right popliteal artery. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed bilateral complete-type PSAs, slender femoral arteries, a right SA aneurysm with thrombosis, and occlusion of the distal SA. Conservative medical treatment was administered owing to advanced age and multiple comorbidities.
CLINICAL DISCUSSION: PSA is prone to complications, including aneurysmal degeneration and thromboembolism. In this case, physical examination revealed a diminished femoral artery pulse and an undetectable dorsalis pedis artery pulse, while the popliteal pulse was not assessed - highlighting the importance of a thorough physical examination for PSA diagnosis. CTA was the key imaging modality for confirming the diagnosis and assessing complications. The patient achieved significant symptomatic improvement with conservative therapy.
CONCLUSION: Clinicians should consider PSA in patients with unexplained lower-limb ischemia. A thorough physical examination, including assessment of the popliteal pulse, is essential for early recognition. CTA is the diagnostic modality of choice. For older patients at high surgical risk, conservative medical treatment remains a safe and effective option.

articles.title: Management of Immune-Mediated Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura Without Plasma Exchange in a Jehovah's Witness: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) is a life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency and is traditionally treated with urgent therapeutic plasma exchange. Management becomes particularly challenging in patients who decline blood products. We report the case of a previously healthy woman with severe iTTP, with a platelet nadir of 6 × 109/L, ADAMTS13 activity < 5%, and an ADAMTS13 inhibitor titer of 2 Bethesda units, who declined plasma exchange because of her religious beliefs as a member of Jehovah's Witnesses. She was treated with high-dose corticosteroids, rituximab, and adjunctive intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Platelet count normalized by hospital Day 9 with progressive resolution of hemolysis, and at 6-month follow-up the patient remained in durable clinical and biochemical remission with normalization of ADAMTS13 activity. This case highlights the potential adjunctive role of IVIG within an immune-directed treatment strategy for iTTP when plasma exchange is not feasible.

articles.title: Immune Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura Presenting With Transient Neurological Deficits: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) is a rare but fatal disorder characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, and ischemic damage of organs due to widespread platelet-rich thrombi in small blood vessels. Early detection and prompt treatment are crucial to reducing mortality.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a female, 66-year-old, who presented with transient episode of left-sided weakness and aphasia that resolved within 30 min. Initial neuroimaging showed no evidence of ischemia. Laboratory evaluation showed severe thrombocytopenia, severe anemia, high lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), reticulocytosis, and the presence of schistocytes in peripheral blood. The calculated PLASMIC score was 6, and ADAMTS13 activity showed severe deficiency, supporting the diagnosis of iTTP. The patient responded well to corticosteroids and therapeutic plasma exchange, with significant clinical and hematological improvement following the treatment. She was discharged after 2 weeks in good condition with a plan for regular follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This case emphasizes the significance of including iTTP in the differential diagnosis of transient neurological attacks in patients with hematological abnormalities. Early initiation of plasma exchange and immunosuppressive therapy are essential to prevent organ damage and further complications.

articles.title: Heavy Metal Toxicity Following Metal-on-Metal Knee Arthroplasty Revision Surgery: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Metallosis is a rare complication; hence, previous investigations regarding this topic are restricted to case reports. Little has been published on metallosis following total knee arthroplasty (TKA). We report the case of a patient who experienced cobalt and chromium metallosis 14 years following TKA-revision surgery. She developed a variety of symptoms that could indicate systemic clinical toxicity, including skin redness, headaches, irritability, cognitive decline, and sleep disturbances. Replacing the prosthesis, utilizing chelation therapy, and trials of double-filtration plasmapheresis reduced the serum level of heavy metals upon regular laboratory follow-ups, leading to a temporary relief of symptoms. The presence of confounding factors and other concomitant conditions makes the distinction between systemic metal exposure and suspected systemic clinical toxicity very challenging.

articles.title: Progressive Ataxia and Cognitive Impairment Associated With SEZ6L2: Serum Neurofilament Light Chain as a Biomarker of Disease Activity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) associated with SEZ6L2 antibodies is a rare neurological disorder characterized by subacute onset of cerebellar ataxia, cognitive dysfunction, and extrapyramidal features. Few cases have been reported, and data on long-term course and treatment response remain limited.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 64-year-old woman developed progressive cerebellar ataxia, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms starting insidiously after SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia in September 2022. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis almost 1 year after onset were unremarkable. Due to progressive symptoms, she was admitted to our department in December 2024. Examination showed severe truncal and gait ataxia, memory impairment, and prominent frontal-executive dysfunction. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral hippocampal T2 hyperintensity with severe medial temporal lobe and cerebellar atrophy. Neuronal antibody testing with a tissue-based assay (TBA) optimized for surface antigens showed strong neuropilar hippocampal and cerebellar staining in serum and CSF. A specific live cell-based assay (CBA) confirmed that the reactivity could be attributed to SEZ6L2 antibodies. Plasmapheresis and high-dose corticosteroids resulted in stabilization of gait impairment and mild cognitive improvement. Longitudinal plasma neurofilament light chain (NFL) monitoring showed initially high levels (85.12 pg/mL), followed by a drastic reduction some months after immunotherapy.
CONCLUSIONS: AE can mimic neurodegenerative processes, and SEZ6L2 antibody testing should be considered in patients with progressive ataxia and limbic involvement, even when no additional clues point towards an autoimmune etiology. Notably, the condition manifested a partial response to immunotherapy, supported by NFL reduction. This suggests that NFL might represent a useful biomarker to monitor disease activity in these conditions.

articles.title: Manganese Dioxide Nanozyme-Integrated Aligned Nanofibers Promote Diabetic Wound Repair through Growth Arrest-Specific Protein 6-Mediated Fibroblast-to-Macrophage Communication.
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds remain difficult to treat because excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), persistent inflammation, and impaired neovascularization collectively hinder tissue repair. Here, we present a bioinspired aligned electrospun nanofiber membrane composed of methacrylated gelatin and o-nitrobenzyl-modified gelatin and functionalized with manganese dioxide (MnO2) nanozymes to regulate the wound microenvironment. Upon hydration and brief ultraviolet irradiation, the membrane forms a conformable nanofibrous hydrogel that closely adapts to irregular wound beds. Among three MnO2 loadings, the formulation containing 180 μg/mL MnO2 was selected as the optimized formulation because it attenuated intracellular ROS while promoting fibroblast proliferation and migration and endothelial angiogenic activity. Mechanistic studies showed that the optimized hydrogel promoted fibroblast secretion of growth arrest-specific protein 6 (Gas6), which attenuated inflammatory macrophage responses and enhanced reparative macrophage responses. Gas6 knockdown weakened these effects, whereas recombinant Gas6 recapitulated them. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified treatment-associated changes in wound cell states and suggested Gas6-associated fibroblast-macrophage communication through computational ligand-receptor analysis. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, the optimized hydrogel accelerated wound closure and enhanced vascularization, re-epithelialization, and collagen remodeling. These findings establish an aligned nanozyme-functionalized nanofibrous hydrogel that links redox regulation to Gas6-associated fibroblast-to-macrophage signaling for diabetic wound repair.

articles.title: Disulfidptosis-Driven Immune-Activated Multimodal Therapy for Glioblastoma with Systemic Safety Control.
articles.abstract: Effective glioblastoma therapy requires simultaneous solutions to poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, insufficient tumor-selective killing, and treatment-related systemic toxicity. We hypothesized that a BBB-penetrating nanoplatform capable of generating distinct H2S exposures in tumor and normal tissues could enhance antitumor efficacy while mitigating doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity. Here, DOX-loaded metastable molybdenum disulfide nanoflowers functionalized with an I6P8 peptide (DOX@MSI) were developed. After BBB transport and tumor accumulation, the acidic, H2O2-rich, and GSH-rich microenvironment accelerates nanoplatform degradation, promoting GSH depletion and enhanced H2S/DOX release. High local H2S upregulates xCT, while H2S/DOX-mediated mitochondrial inhibition suppresses NADPH regeneration, synergistically triggering disulfidptosis. Meanwhile, H2S suppresses the JAK2/STAT3/IDO axis, alleviating DOX-induced immunosuppression and enhancing immunogenic cell death and T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. In contrast, slower degradation under physiological conditions enables sustained low-level H2S release, reducing the level of oxidative stress and ERK-associated apoptosis in cardiomyocytes. Together with NIR-enhanced photothermal therapy, DOX@MSI suppresses orthotopic glioblastoma while reducing cardiac injury, thereby integrating tumor-selective multimodal therapy with active organ protection.

articles.title: Diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for pediatric cerebral malaria: a review.
articles.abstract: Pediatric cerebral malaria (PCM) kills 15% to 25% of the African children in whom it is diagnosed and leaves many survivors with neurocognitive deficits. It is a disease of the cerebral microvasculature whose pathogenic sequence is now partly resolved at the molecular level. Plasmodium falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 binds a broad range of endothelial cell receptors, of which binding to the endothelial protein C receptor, in some cases together with intercellular adhesion molecule 1, is the combination linked to severe and cerebral disease. CD36 is the receptor most commonly used by field isolates but is associated with uncomplicated malaria, at least two dozen further receptors have been described for parasitized erythrocytes, and a PfEMP1 binding domain has been identified for only a few of them. The ensuing endothelial activation releases von Willebrand factor and angiopoietin-2 and disables Tie - 2 signaling. Free heme, delivered in part by histidine-rich protein 2 nanoparticles internalized by caveolin-1-dependent endocytosis, is proposed to engage two separable innate arms, one through stimulator of interferon genes 1 (STING1) yielding type I interferon and CXCL10, the other through NLRP3 and caspase - 1 yielding interleukin-1-beta; the first was shown in murine brain endothelium and the second in a human cerebral endothelial cell line, and the two have not been demonstrated in one system. Junctional remodeling and ephrin type-A receptor 2 signaling open the blood-brain barrier in murine models, barrier disruption is documented histologically in human autopsy series, and neuronal and axonal proteins reach the circulation of affected children. The sequence summarized here therefore combines links established in human disease with links that remain experimental or proposed, and the review marks which is which at each step. This review treats candidate biomarkers as readouts of that cascade rather than as free-standing correlates. Because the clinical definition cannot separate malaria-attributable coma from coma with incidental parasitemia, we appraise malarial retinopathy as the in vivo reference standard and set out why a negative result is heterogeneous. Parasite-derived and host-derived markers are mapped onto those steps, with attention to the few evaluated against non-malarial coma rather than against milder malaria, and to what a marker adds at the bedside. Extracellular vesicles and microRNAs are assessed as emerging platforms. We close on druggable nodes in the cascade and on using molecular readouts to stratify children for host-directed therapy.

articles.title: Three-Dimensional Immunofluorescence Analysis of Psoriatic Plaques Before and After Pulsed Dye Laser Treatment: Reduced T-Cell Content Without Changes in Nerve Fiber or Blood Vessel Density.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pulsed dye laser (PDL) treatment for psoriasis has demonstrated its potential for treatment-free remission periods exceeding 1 year. The mechanism leading to remission is not fully understood, but PDL is known to heat the vasculature in the skin. We hypothesized that heat diffuses from the vasculature to the surrounding environment, including perivascular nerves and T-cells, leading to an interruption of the neurogenic inflammatory cycle that drives psoriasis.
METHODS: We compared histological features of the vasculature, nerves, and leukocyte infiltrate in 120 biopsy sections (80 µm thick) from 20 patients, collected before and after two PDL treatments. The alterations in vasculature were categorized into three distinct classifications: papillary vasculature, reticular vasculature, and total vasculature. Nerve fibers were divided into free epidermal nerve fibers, perivascular nerve fibers around capillaries, and reticular nerves. The densities of these structures, as well as the volume of the epidermal and dermal leukocyte infiltrate, were calculated from the three-dimensional (3D) fluorescence microscopy images.
RESULTS: Two sessions of PDL treatment significantly reduced CD3+ leukocyte infiltrate in the skin. Furthermore, pruritus and epidermal thickness were also significantly reduced. Vascular and nerve fiber density did not significantly differ before and after two treatments.
CONCLUSIONS: Using 3D immunofluorescence microscopy to quantify T-cells, vasculature and nerve fibers, we found that two PDL treatments were associated with a significant reduction in CD3+ T-cells, even in patients whose clinical severity did not improve, while vascular and nerve fiber density remained unchanged. Perivascular heat diffusion and potential alterations in vascular integrity may contribute to this reduction, but this hypothesis requires confirmation in future studies.

articles.title: Lymphopenia and Circulating Biomarker Dynamics Associated with Clinical Outcome and Toxicity in Pazopanib-Treated Radioiodine-Refractory Thyroid Cancer: Exploratory Analyses from the Pazothyr Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pazopanib showed clinical activity in progressive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid carcinoma (RAIR-DTC), although its use is limited by substantial toxicity not reduced by intermittent treatment. We aimed to identify biomarkers associated with outcome and treatment-related toxicity in these patients.
METHODS: This study reported exploratory results related to the Pazothyr trial (NCT01813136) investigating pazopanib efficacy in RAIR-DTC patients. We evaluated lymphopenia and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) from the Pazothyr clinical database (n = 168). Dedicated informed consent for additional plasma and tumor sample collection allowed quantification of plasma angiogenic factors and cytokines at baseline and after one month of pazopanib (n = 111). Immune markers (CD8, FOXP3, CD163, and PDL1) analyzed by immunohistochemistry in archived primary tumors from patients (n = 68) with response or stable disease after 6 months of pazopanib were scored semiquantitatively. Associations with response, progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and substantial treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were evaluated. Given the exploratory nature of this study, no adjustment for multiple comparisons was performed.
RESULTS: At baseline, moderate and severe lymphopenia were associated with shorter PFS, unlike high NLR. Elevated Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A (VEGF-A), Interleukin 6 (IL-6), and CXCL8 correlated with poorer PFS. High VEGF-A, hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), IL-6, CXCL8, and CXCL9 were associated with shorter OS. X Early changes in placental growth factor (PlGF), HGF, interleukin 12 subunit p40, and CXCL10 were associated with substantial TRAEs. Multivariable analyses identified baseline severe lymphopenia (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.39 [confidence interval or CI 1.27-4.48], p = 0.007) and high CXCL8 (HR = 2.01 [CI 1.26-3.21], p = 0.004) as independent factors associated with progression. High baseline NLR (HR = 2.26 [CI 1.21-4.22], p = 0.01), HGF (HR = 2.37 [CI 1.33-4.20], p = 0.003), and CXCL8 (HR = 2.20 [CI 1.25-3.87], p = 0.006) were similarly associated with death. One-month increases in PlGF (odds ratio [OR] = 2.49 [CI 1.13-5.50], p = 0.024) and HGF (OR = 2.91 [CI 1.32-6.43], p = 0.008) were independently associated with substantial TRAEs. In patients with tumor samples, Programmed cell Death-Ligand 1 (PDL1)-immune cell score (ICS) >1% (HR = 2.05 [CI 1.15-3.66], p = 0.015) was also associated with progression.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline lymphopenia and inflammatory plasma biomarkers were associated with clinical outcome, whereas early changes in circulating factors were associated with substantial TRAEs. These exploratory results require prospective validation in RAIR-DTC patients treated with pazopanib or other VEGF receptor-targeting multikinase inhibitors. The relevance of PDL1-ICS expression for anti-PD1/PDL1-based therapies requires dedicated prospective trials.

articles.title: HuR Inhibition Attenuates Hypertension and Fibrosis in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upregulation of the RNA-binding protein HuR (human antigen R) has been reported in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but its pathogenic role remains incompletely understood. We hypothesized that HuR promotes renal and vascular injury in hypertensive CKD and that pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates disease progression. We therefore investigated the role of HuR in deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) plus Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced CKD and evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of the HuR inhibitor, KH3 .
METHODS: Male mice underwent uninephrectomy followed by DOCA+Ang II infusion with 1% NaCl in drinking water and were treated with KH3 or vehicle for 3 weeks. Control mice received saline without DOCA or Ang II.
RESULTS: DOCA+Ang II markedly increased HuR expression in circulating exosomes and kidney tissues, which was attenuated by KH3 treatment. KH3 reduced albuminuria, improved renal function, and attenuated kidney hypertrophy, glomerular, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis. These renoprotective effects were associated with reduced podocyte and tubular injury, decreased macrophage infiltration, and suppression of NF-κB (nuclear factor-kappa B) p65, Nox2 (NADPH oxidase 2), AKT (protein kinase B) phosphorylation, TGFβ1 (transforming growth factor β1), and Wisp1 (WNT1-inducible signaling pathway protein 1) signaling. KH3 also partially lowered arterial blood pressure in DOCA+Ang II-treated mice. Further studies in vascular smooth muscle cells and mesenteric resistance arteries suggested that HuR inhibition may suppress vascular profibrotic signaling associated with SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2).
CONCLUSIONS: HuR is upregulated in renal and vascular tissues in DOCA+Ang II-induced CKD and contributes to renal inflammation, oxidative stress, fibrosis, and vascular dysfunction. Pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates renal and vascular injury, supporting HuR as a promising therapeutic target for CKD.

articles.title: Collagen-Functionalized hydroxyapatite promotes biointegration and vascularization of xenogeneic bone grafts by modulating macrophage polarization.
articles.abstract: Background: In periodontal and bone-defect reconstruction, bovine-derived hydroxyapatite (HA) is widely utilized as a xenogeneic bone graft material. However, its inherent propensity to elicit a foreign body reaction (FBR) often results in a dense fibrous encapsulation at the host-material interface, thereby impeding early vascular ingrowth and integration associated with new bone formation and limiting its efficacy in complex bone defects.Objective: This study aimed to construct a biomimetic type I collagen (Col) coating on HA (HA + Col) and determine whether it reshapes the host-material immune microenvironment.Methods: Using a rat subcutaneous implantation model, we comparatively evaluated immunomodulatory performance and histological outcomes at an acute inflammatory time point (day 2) and a tissue remodeling time point (day 28).Results: Collagen modification markedly altered the nanoscale surface morphology and effectively suppressed excessive inflammatory cell infiltration at early stages. Immunohistochemical and histological analyses showed that HA + Col was associated with shift of macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like profile (iNOS+) toward a pro-resolving/pro-reparative M2-like profile (CD163+). At day 28, compared with unmodified HA, HA + Col significantly reduced fibrous capsule thickness and increased the neovascular area in subcutaneous tissue. Goldner trichrome staining further confirmed improved soft-tissue integration and collagen deposition quality in the HA + Col group. Collectively, collagen functionalization confers immunomodulatory activity to HA, mitigating FBR and establishing an osteoimmune microenvironment favorable for vascularization and soft-tissue integration in subcutaneous tissue.Conclusion: These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for future evaluation of functionalized bone graft substitutes in bone-defect models.[Formula: see text].

articles.title: Stage-Adaptive Bilayer Hydrogel Coordinates Photodynamic Antibacterial Therapy with Engineered Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated Immunomodulation in Infected Diabetic Wounds.
articles.abstract: During the early phase of treatment, infected diabetic wounds require rapid bacterial control, whereas subsequent healing benefits from relief of persistent oxidative stress and inflammation, resulting in distinct and partly opposing redox demands over time. We therefore developed a stage-adaptive bilayer hydrogel that separates photodynamic antibacterial therapy from engineered small extracellular vesicle (sEV) delivery. The wound-contacting layer contains chlorin e6 (Ce6), while the ROS-responsive upper layer scavenges ROS and retains miR-146a-enriched sEVs carrying a human CD64-recognition module. The bilayer architecture limited premature release of sEV-associated particles during photodynamic treatment but allowed substantial release thereafter, with key vesicle-associated features preserved after irradiation. In human macrophages, engineered sEVs increased intracellular miR-146a, reduced IRAK1 abundance and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation, decreased CD86, and increased CD206. These effects were partly weakened by CD64 blockade. In infected diabetic wounds, Bil-Gel@miR-sEVs reduced bacterial burden and oxidative stress, suppressed IRAK1/NF-κB-associated inflammatory signaling, shifted macrophage-associated markers toward a repair-associated pattern, and improved epithelial, vascular, and matrix reconstruction. This bilayer design therefore links early infection control with later immunoregulation and tissue repair within one biomaterial.

articles.title: Beyond Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen: The Design and Future of Novel Radiopharmaceuticals Targeting the Tumor Microenvironment.
articles.abstract: Targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy has entered mainstream oncology through the clinical success of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-directed imaging and [177Lu] Lu-PSMA-617 therapy. However, heterogeneous antigen expression, acquired resistance, lineage plasticity, and nonresponding lesions show that a cancer cell-centric strategy cannot fully address the ecological complexity of advanced malignancy. The tumor microenvironment (TME) offers a complementary target space because stromal, vascular, immune, and chemokine-driven niches are functionally required for tumor growth and are often more genomically stable than malignant cells. This review synthesizes the biological rationale, radiochemical design, clinical translation, and current limitations of TME-targeted radiopharmaceuticals, focusing on fibroblast activation protein (FAP), integrins, and the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis. The authors discuss first-generation FAP inhibitor (FAPI) tracers and therapeutic limitations caused by short tumor residence, and then compare next-generation strategies, including dimerization, multimerization, albumin-binding motifs, peptide-based ligands such as FAP-2286, and newer FAPI-derived therapeutic constructs. They also reassess RGD-based integrin targeting as a clinically informative but heterogeneous angiogenesis platform, and summarize CXCR4-directed pentixather therapy in hematological malignancies and selected solid tumor models. Finally, they examine radionuclide selection, dosimetry, patient selection, and combination strategies with chemotherapy, antiangiogenic therapy, immune checkpoint blockade, cytokine therapy, and cell-based therapy. TME-targeted radiopharmaceuticals are unlikely to replace tumor cell-directed theranostics; rather, their most important role may be to reshape resistant tumor ecosystems and rationally extend precision radionuclide therapy beyond single-antigen paradigms.

articles.title: Neuromelanins: a link between brain aging and neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.abstract: Neuromelanins (NMs) accumulate in large amounts in catecholaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra (SN) and locus coeruleus (LC), which selectively degenerate in Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Lower amounts of NMs are also present in other human brain regions. NMs are contained in specialized autolysosomes with lipid bodies, proteins, and metals. Their structure, synthesis, functions, and cellular localization differ from those of melanins in non-nervous tissues. Purified NMs have a complex structure, are composed of melanic moieties, lipids, proteins, and inorganic components, and are insoluble. NMs can exert either a protective or toxic role depending on cellular context. NMs synthesis is driven by cytosolic catecholamines and is a protective process, as it removes excess cytosolic catechols that would otherwise trigger neurotoxicity. NMs can bind reactive/toxic metals, forming stable and non-toxic complexes, thereby playing a neuroprotective role. However, NMs released from degenerating neurons in PD and AD activate microglia, which release reactive species and proinflammatory factors, thereby exacerbating neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. The major histocompatibility complex class I is present within NM-containing organelles of SN and LC neurons and can bind antigens, presenting them on the neuronal membrane. Subsequently, CD8+ T-cells may target catecholaminergic NM-containing neurons, contributing to neurodegeneration. The loss of NM-containing neurons in PD and AD causes a decrease of NMs concentration within the SN and LC, which can be visualized using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). NM-sensitive MRI of the SN and LC is increasingly being used for the diagnosis and treatment monitoring of neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders.

articles.title: Contemporary Management of Arteriovenous Malformations.
articles.abstract: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are congenital, high-flow vascular anomalies that disrupt normal blood flow by forming direct connections between arteries and veins. While rare, AVMs in the hand and wrist present unique clinical challenges due to the region's anatomic complexity and functional importance. This review highlights modern diagnostic tools, therapeutic strategies, and multidisciplinary approaches that shape contemporary AVM care, with an emphasis on improving functional outcomes and patient quality of life.

articles.title: [Entrapment of the ulnar nerve at the Guyon's canal].
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: The ulnar nerve runs at the level of the ulnar carpus through Guyon's canal. Due to the proximity to very rigid ligamentous and bony structures, space-occupying processes or fractures can easily cause compression of the ulnar nerve and its two distal branches. Pathologies of the adjacent ulnar artery can also irritate the nerve.
ABSTRACT: After cubital tunnel syndrome, this is the second most common compression syndrome of the ulnar nerve. Overall, compression at Guyon´s canal is a very rare condition, which is considered challenging due to its variability of symptoms. Since the ulnar nerve divides within Guyon's canal into its two end branches, the superficial branch and the deep branch, the clinical manifestation of nerve compression can present with mixed sensorimotor, purely sensory, or purely motor deficits.
ABSTRACT: The most common causes of compression neuropathy include ganglion cysts, aberrant muscles, fractures, or vascular anomalies within Guyon's canal. Therefore, in addition to an thorough clinical examination, the preoperative workout should also include appropriate imaging modalities (X-ray, MRI, CT, or ultrasound) as well as a neurological and electrophysiological evaluation.
ABSTRACT: Surgical exploration and decompression of the nerve at all potential sites of compression is indicated if symptoms persist or if sensorimotor deficits have existed for a longer time, in order to prevent irreversible late sequelae.

articles.title: An ulcerative colitis taxonomy defined by individual patient-reported response trajectories.
articles.abstract: A barrier to precision medicine for ulcerative colitis (UC) is the inability to predict and mechanistically explain treatment responses. Using patient-reported outcomes (PROs) from a phase 3b comparative trial of 768 participants, we identified four distinct patient response-trajectory groups for vedolizumab (anti-integrin) and adalimumab (antitumor necrosis factor). Validation in a second phase 3 trial of 576 participants linked PRO-defined vedolizumab trajectories to long-term disease complications. Bulk, single cell, and spatial transcriptomics and proteomics identified vascular inflammation as associated with vedolizumab nonresponse through interactions between SPP1+ macrophages and endothelial cells. In two separate real-world cohorts of 4,981 and 3,854 patients with UC, concomitant use of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (modulators of vascular inflammation) was associated with reduced long-term complications for vedolizumab but not anticytokine therapies. These findings define a response-trajectory-based taxonomy that requires prospective validation for clinical utility and applications for selecting vedolizumab combination therapy in UC.
